candidate_relations.label: Campylobacter jejuni enteritis with pancolitis
candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record confirms Campylobacter jejuni as the causative organism and pancolitis on CT, but the benchmark reference is toxic megacolon — a specific life-threatening complication defined by colonic dilation (transverse and descending colon dilation on AXR), systemic toxicity (fever 38.4°C, leukocytosis 16×10^9/L, markedly elevated CRP 429.8 mg/L, hypoalbuminaemia, tachypnoea), and the absence of obstruction/perforation. C001 names the underlying cause and colonic inflammation but omits the toxic megacolon complication that is the required final diagnostic object.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies the etiology and colonic inflammation but does not capture the specific complication of toxic megacolon, which is the requested final diagnostic object

case_quality_flags: Toxic megacolon secondary to Campylobacter jejuni is rare but supported by colonic dilation on AXR plus systemic toxicity criteria; reference diagnosis is clinically defensible given the imaging and laboratory findings.
